report:
- The study reveals severe full thickness cartilage degeneration of medial tibial plateau and medial femoral condyle, measured about 2.2 cm and 2.3 cm in length, respectively. Thin cartilage degeneration with focal delamination tear of anterior aspect of lateral tibial plateau, measured about intact8 cm in length. There are bilateral marginal osteophytes and no subchondral bone change. The thin cartilage degeneration with fissuring surface of medial and lateral side of patella and trochlea and narrowing of patellofemoral joint is noted. Overall findings are suggested degenerative change of knee. 
 - There are multiple loose bodies which one ossified lesion at medial side of capsule, measured about 1.2 cm, and three calcified lesions at anteromedial, posteromedial and posterosuperior medial side of capsule are seen, measured up to intact8 cm. 
  
 Central supporting system  
 - Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): There is enlarged and mucoid degenerative change is noted.  
 - Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  
 - No evidence of anterior tibial translation is noted.  
  
 Medial compartment  
 - Medial meniscus: Mild bulging with horizontal tear at body and posterior horn and radial tear at posterior horn and posterior root are noted. 
 - Medial collateral ligament: Intact. 
 - Medial tibial plateau: Normal.  
 - Medial femoral condyle: Normal.  
  
 Lateral compartment  
 - Lateral meniscus: Myxoid degenerative change without definite tear. 
 - Iliotibial band: Normal.  
 - Lateral collateral ligament: Mild increased SI without definite tear.  
 - Popliteus tendon: Increased SI with minimal fluid. 
 - Popliteofibular ligament: Normal.  
 - Biceps femoris tendon : Preserved.  
 - Lateral tibial plateau: Normal.  
 - Lateral femoral condyle: Normal.  
  
 Patellofemoral compartment  
 - Quadriceps tendon: Normal.  
 - Patellar tendon: Normal with mild subcutaneous edema.  
 - Medial patellar retinaculum:Normal. 
 - Lateral patellar retinaculum: Normal.  
  
 Others  
 - Effusion within tibiofemoral joint and patellofemoral jont extending along suprapatellar bursa is observed. Associated thickening of synovial lining along these sites are noted; likely synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis.  
 - Muscle bulks grade I at tibialis anterior, fibularis longus, extensor digitorum longus and grade II of vartus muscles are noted. 
 - Neurovascular bundles are intact.   - Degenerative change of right knee. 
 - Stained of lateral collateral ligament and popliteal tendon. 
 - Effusion within tibiofemoral joint and patellofemoral jont extending along suprapatellar bursa associated thickening of synovial lining along these sites; likely synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis.

The study reveals normal knee joint alignment.   No fracture is seen.  
  Minimal amount of joint effusion is seen.  
  MCL is intact.  Medial meniscus is not torn.  
  FCL, popliteus and biceps femoris tendons are preserved.       
  There is small size posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with suspected anteriorly flipped displaced meniscal fragment closed to the anterior horn. 
  Focal high grade partial thickness cartilage defect, about 6.5x17mm. at posterior part of the lateral meniscus, without subchondral bone lesion, is detected. 
 Normal course with preserved signal of the ACL is noted.  The PCL is intact.  
 The PF joint surface is preserved.   No subchondral bone lesion is noted.  
 The quadriceps and patellar tendons are preserved.     Evidence tear at posterior horn of the lateral meniscus with anteriorly flipped meniscal fragment closed to the anterior horn. 
  High grade, partial thickness cartilage defect, about 6.5x17mm. at posterior part of the lateral meniscus, without subchondral bone lesion.

Indication: Right knee sprain
Comparison: X-ray of the right knee [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Fragmentation of the tibial tuberosity, compatible with remote Osgood-Schlatter. Mild bone marrow edema between fragments and the dominant component of the tibial tuberosity likely represents a superimposed osseous stress response. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Increased signal in the body and posterior horn which is not meet criteria for tear and likely represents remnant of vascularity.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 6 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

Sequelae of remote Osgood Schlatter disease with mild superimposed osseous stress response between the tibial tuberosity and adjacent bone fragment.

In the medial compartment, there are abnormal shape and signal of posterior horn; suspect tear of posterior horn of the medial meniscus.  There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury.  
  
 The lateral compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury.  
  
 The patellofemoral joint, intact trochlea. The patellar cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is high grade almost complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at distal part (near tibia). The posterior cruciate ligament is focal buckling at midsubstance . There is no anterior anterior tibial translation.  
  
 There is grade I ligamentous sprain of the medial collateral ligament. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. 
  
 Focal linear bone marrow edema at mid tibial plateau, near tibial spine  ACL; high grade almost complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at distal part (near tibia).  
  PCL; focal buckling at midsubstance 
  Focal linear bone marrow edema at mid tibial plateau, near tibial spine  
  Medical menisucs; suspect tear of posterior horn of the medial meniscus

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. Large intra-articular organized soft tissue hematoma measuring 5.2 x 1.5 x 5.8 cm.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with full-thickness tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild loss of substance of the posterior horn.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Complete avulsion of the biceps femoris from the fibular head associated with a large multiloculated soft tissue hematoma surrounding the tear extending along the lateral gastrocnemius muscle.
Complete avulsion of the popliteus tendon at its insertion on the lateral femoral condyle.
Severe edema and irregularity of the lateral collateral ligament proper with high-grade partial-thickness tear from its femoral attachment and complete avulsion from its fibular attachment.
No fracture of the fibular head is identified.

Longitudinal vertical tear of the peripheral posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus.
Diffuse chondral thinning without deep fissuring.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Avulsion of the posterior cruciate ligament from its femoral attachment.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Normal.

Bones:
Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Diffuse edema of the visualized proximal anterior compartment of the leg muscles. Associated diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.Sequela of knee dislocation with complete tears of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments.
2.Extensive injury of the posterolateral corner with complete avulsion of the lateral collateral ligament proper, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon as described above.
3.High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with complete tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
4.Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild substance loss of the posterior horn.
5.Longitudinal vertical peripheral tear of the posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus compatible with a Wrisberg rip.
6.Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.
7.Diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting low-grade traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection. Associated denervation edema of the visualized anterior muscle compartment of the proximal leg.
8.Moderate knee joint effusion with large intra-articular organized hematoma

Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial. El
resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y patelofemorales sin alteraciones.
Leve derrame articular con discreta sinovitis difusa. Pequeño quiste poplíteo no complicado.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura. Tendón rotuliano,
tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Menisco lateral de morfología discoidea con extensa rotura y segmento parcialmente desplazado hacia la
región intercondílea posterior.
Rotura compleja de la raíz meniscal posterior, cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco medial con
moderada extrusión y edema de las partes blandas adyacentes.
Edema óseo difuso del cóndilo femoral medial con imagen sugerente de fractura subcortical en zona de
carga anterior, sin colapso articular, con edema las partes blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la región central del cóndilo femoral medial.
Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo complicado.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal.
